To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a high variability within one bamboo culm, (2) the cell walls of fibres and parenchyms are thicker in culms of higher age, (3) there is no significant difference between fibre and parenchyme cell wall thickness, and (4) the cell walls are not significantly thicker at the base than at the top of the culms.

the bamboo culm wall thickness of both fibres and parenchyms cells increase with age, and that the cell wall thickening is not uniform within the culm, but that the highest mean values of cell wall thickening are recorded in culms that are at least 3 years old.

the cell wall of fibres and parenchyms of Phyllostachys and Dendrocallamus culms is thickening during the first year, and that the wall of fibres of Phyllostackys and Dendrocolumas is thickening in later years.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a great variability of cell wall thickness and wall layering pattern within one bamboo culm, which is in contrast with the common belief that bamboo cell walls are fully matured within 1 year after the culm is initiated.
the fact that bamboo culms of 1 year old or older can be harvested for wood products, as they have reached the highest mean fibre and parenchycha wall thicknesses.
the fact that cell wall thickening of bamboo culms is not a uniform process but a highly variable one.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bamboo fibres are not thickening in a linear way during the life span of the culms but that there is a significant increase in cell wall thickness in the first year after culm emergence, followed by a more or less steady cell wall thickness until the age of about 1.5 years.
bamboo culms are not suitable for industrial use because of their low fibre wall thickness.
the bamboo culm is not a homogeneous material with respect to cell wall thickness and that cell wall thickening of bamboo fibres is a continuous process throughout the lifetime of the culm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell wall maturing is not restricted to the first year of growth, but continues for a few years, and the process is more complex than previously thought.
the wall thickening of fibres in bamboo culms is a slow and continuous process, but that the highest values for wall thickness are reached at higher ages.

the bamboo cell wall thickness of the fibres and parenchyms in a culm is highly variable, but that the wall thickening of both cell types increases with age, although the rate of thickening decreases with time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bamboo cell wall is a highly dynamic structure that is still thickening and maturing at least during the first years of its life.

the bamboo culm can be regarded as a composite structure with a high variability in cell wall thickness within one culm, which is masking the fact that cell wall thickening can take place during a longer period of time.
bamboo culms should be harvested when the bamboo is at least 44 months old.
